sections.heading: What Is the Biggest Problem With Metal Roofs?

c.v: The biggest problem with metal roofs is movement: metal expands and contracts with every temperature swing, and that movement works on the fasteners, sealants, and seams.

runs.v: On an exposed-fastener roof, the washer seals under thousands of screws dry out and the screws back out, and sealant at metal laps typically fails in 5 to 10 years; on standing seam, seam failures show up where panels were fastened too rigidly to move. Newark roofs typically see 30–50 freeze-thaw cycles each winter, and freeze-thaw cycling pumps water into any gap a seal leaves open, while on a summer afternoon a dark roof surface can exceed 160°F, so a dark metal panel can swing through well over 100 degrees in a year.

The other problems are smaller but real. Cut edges and scratches rust when the coating is broken, copper runoff onto galvanized steel or aluminum causes galvanic corrosion, oil-canning makes flat panels look wavy, and condensation forms under a metal cover when the attic is poorly ventilated. Metal roofs also cost more to install than asphalt shingles, and roof issues on metal need expert roof repair from a crew that knows the specific panel system, because a standing-seam panel and an exposed-fastener panel take different repair methods; a tube of caulk over a failed seam is how small roof leaks become structural damage to the deck. None of these problems is a reason to avoid metal; each is a reason to install it correctly and inspect it. A roof inspection should occur twice a year, in spring after the cold winters and in fall before them, and regular roof inspections can prevent costly repairs later.

When a metal roof is leaking now, the fix starts the same way on every roof type. Newark Quality Roofing's emergency roof repair services are available 24/7 and target a 1–4 hour emergency response: roof leak repair often starts with emergency tarping, which stops active water entry during urgent repairs, and emergency roofing services help prevent further damage to homes before the permanent repair. An active roof leak on metal usually traces to a lifted seam, a backed-out fastener, or a flashing joint, and flashing repairs are crucial for preventing leaks at roof-to-wall transitions. Trusted contractors provide detailed written estimates for emergency repairs, separating the stabilization from the permanent fix, and storm damage repair restores the components damaged by severe weather, not only the hole that leaked.

sections.heading: What Is the 25% Rule for Roofing?

c.v: The 25% rule for roofing says that once damage reaches about a quarter of the roof, a full roof replacement usually returns more than another repair.

runs.v: For metal, the contractor-consensus thresholds are 20 to 25% panel corrosion or 25% seam-connection damage, per roofing industry guidance; below them, most repairs are local: reseal the seam, replace the fasteners, or swap the corroded panel section. New Jersey also has a code version of the rule: under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in a 12-month period on a commercial building requires a construction permit, so a commercial roof replacement is a permitted job, while a re-roof of a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance.

Roof replacement is necessary when damage exceeds repair limits, and the roof repair process is different from the replacement process. Roof replacement involves removing the old roof and inspecting the deck: the tear-off exposes the roof deck, rotted sheathing is replaced as part of ensuring structural integrity, and the new metal goes on over an ice barrier and a high-temperature underlayment. On an asphalt roof, granule loss exceeding 30% indicates a roof past repair and in need of replacement, and that is a natural point to weigh switching from asphalt shingles to metal. A detailed repair plan puts the roof's condition, the repair-or-replace recommendation, and the price in writing before any work begins, which keeps a small repair from turning into costly repairs later.

sections.heading: Metal Roofing vs. Other Roofing Systems in Newark's Climate

c.v: Metal roofs can last 40–70 years depending on the material, and proper installation and maintenance can extend metal roofing lifespan beyond 40 years, which puts metal ahead of most other roofing systems on a Newark home.

runs.v: The InterNACHI chart puts metal at 40 to 80 years, while asphalt shingles last 20–30 years with proper maintenance, EPDM roofs typically last 15–25 years, tile roofs can last over 50 years with proper care, and slate roofs are known for their lifetime durability. Metal roofing requires fewer repairs over its service life compared to some other materials, because metal roofs resist cracking, rotting, and various forms of weather damage.

Newark's climate tests every roof type. Cold winters bring snow loads and 30–50 freeze-thaw cycles, nor'easters bring heavy rain and wind-driven rain that can penetrate beneath lifted shingles in Newark, and summer sun can push a dark roof surface past 160°F. Metal roofs handle heavy rain, high winds, and snow loads exceptionally well, shed snow quickly, and have no granules or mat to wear away, which is why metal roofing is increasingly popular in northern New Jersey due to its durability against harsh weather. Ice dams frequently form on older homes with poor attic insulation, and proper attic ventilation prevents ice dam formation under metal as well as under shingles.

Energy efficiency is the second advantage. Metal reflects solar radiant heat rather than absorbing it, which can reduce cooling costs by 10% to 25%, and energy-efficient metal roofs with reflective finishes lower cooling costs most during warmer months. Metal roofs typically carry a high Class A fire rating against burning embers or sparks, and most metal roofing materials are non-combustible, which adds protection where Newark houses stand close together. Metal roofing materials are 100% recyclable at the end of their lifespan and often contain recycled content, so an old metal roof leaves the site as scrap rather than landfill.

sections.heading: Metal Roof Installation and Repair FAQs

faqs.q: How long does a metal roof last in the New Jersey climate?

runs.v: A metal roof lasts 40 to 80 years, with copper at 70-plus years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, against 20 years for 3-tab asphalt and 30 years for architectural asphalt. Proper attic ventilation extends roof life by up to 25%, per the NRCA, and standing-seam panels outlast exposed-fastener systems.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace a metal roof?

runs.v: Repair a metal roof when the damage stays localized at seams, fasteners, or a small section. Replace it when panel corrosion exceeds 20 to 25% of the area or seam-connection damage exceeds 25%, the contractor-consensus thresholds, per roofing industry guidance.

faqs.q: How much does metal roof repair cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Metal roof repair runs $200–$1,000 for a minor leak and up to $3,000 for severe corrosion, with a seam re-weld at $250–$1,100 and fastener fixes at $150–$1,000. A full metal install costs $9.00–$16.00 per square foot in New Jersey, and Newark Quality Roofing provides a free written estimate.

faqs.q: What is the difference between standing-seam and metal-shingle roofing?

runs.v: Standing-seam roofing runs continuous concealed-fastener panels from ridge to eave on clips that let the metal move, while metal-shingle roofing fits stamped exposed-fastener panels that replicate slate, shake, and tile. Standing seam develops fewer leaks; metal shingles suit homes where curb appeal calls for a traditional look.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a metal roof in Newark, NJ?

runs.v: A re-roof of the roof covering on a detached one- and two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and requires no construction permit. A commercial roof replacement, or repairs to more than 25% of a commercial roof in 12 months, needs a permit, as does any structural change to the rafters or trusses.

faqs.q: Can a metal roof be installed over existing asphalt shingles?

runs.v: Yes, over a single layer: a metal roof installs over one layer of existing asphalt shingles on a batten system that creates an air space. When the deck carries 2 or more layers or hides damage, the old roof comes off first so the roof deck can be inspected and repaired.

faqs.q: Why does a metal roof oil-can or buckle?

runs.v: A metal roof oil-cans or buckles when thermal expansion stresses a panel fastened without adequate movement, the failure a clip-based standing-seam system prevents. Oil-canning is mostly cosmetic, but buckled panels can open seams and should be inspected.

faqs.q: What is the average cost to install a metal roof?

runs.v: In New Jersey, a metal roof install runs $9.00–$16.00 per square foot, so a 1,500-square-foot roof typically costs about $13,500–$24,000 and a 2,000-square-foot roof about $18,000–$32,000. Standing seam, copper, and complex roof shapes sit at the top of that range.

faqs.q: Are metal roofs noisy in the rain?

runs.v: Not over a solid deck. Installed over sheathing, underlayment, and an insulated attic, a metal roof is typically no louder in heavy rain than other roofing systems; the drumming people remember comes from metal fastened over open framing on barns and sheds.

No. A metal roof does not make a lightning strike more likely, and the metal itself is non-combustible. Buildings that need lightning protection get a separate lightning protection system, whatever the roof type.

Steel panels are protected by a zinc or aluminum-zinc coating plus paint, so rust starts only where that protection is broken, usually at cut edges, scratches, or under copper runoff. Aluminum and copper do not rust; they form a protective oxide or patina, which is why aluminum is often chosen for exposure to salt air.
